### P4 "Integrate" (Compute Shader) · Compute

description: Velocity-to-position integrator. Applies position += velocity * TIMEDELTA (symplectic Euler). Place this at the END of a force chain — after all force shaders have accumulated their contributions into velocity — and before the renderer. Do NOT use together with self-contained simulations (NBodyGravity, SpringMass, RigidBodyBasic) which already do their own integration.; categories: Forces; resources: geo:geometry, timeScale:float

```glsl
// Frame time step, clamped to [0, 0.1 s] (10 fps worst case). A clock jump -- a seek, a loop, a
// hitch, or a stepped render interleaved with the transport -- delivers a
// TIMEDELTA of seconds, or a negative one, and an explicit integrator then
// flings every particle away or runs it backwards. Clamping is the standard
// guard (G. Fiedler, "Fix Your Timestep!", 2004).
float stepDt() { return clamp(TIMEDELTA, 0.0, 0.1); }

void main()
// … 13 more lines
```

### P5 "BasicForces.1" (Compute Shader) · Compute

description: Basic velocity modifiers, one per forceType. Drag: velocity loses the fraction drag every 1/60 s. Speed Limit: speed clamped between minSpeed and maxSpeed (a resting particle gets a random push to minSpeed). Spring: pulled toward springTarget with springStiffness, damped by springDamping. ### P7 "VortexForce" (Compute Shader) · Compute

description: Vortex force — particles rotate around a configurable axis with radial falloff. Classic spiral/tornado/galaxy-arm effect. The radial strength lets you combine rotation with inward pull (tornado) or outward push (explosion ring).
